module.purpose: Defines configuration, migration processing, identifier creation, and type guards for custom record types integrated into the tldraw store schema.
module.summary: This module provides the public and internal utilities needed to register custom records, create their record types, normalize migration definitions, generate migration identifiers, and construct or validate typed record IDs. It supports document, session, and presence scopes, optional default properties, full or simplified migration sequences, and record-specific filtering during migration.
module.businessContext: Supports application-specific data such as comments, annotations, and custom state within tldraw persistence and synchronization. Failures can prevent custom records from being created, validated, migrated, or synchronized correctly.

typeShapes.name: CustomRecordInfo
typeShapes.shape:
{
	/**
	 * The scope determines how records of this type are persisted and synchronized:
	 * - **document**: Persisted and synced across all clients
	 * - **session**: Local to current session, not synced
	 * - **presence**: Ephemeral presence data, may be synced but not persisted
	 */
	scope: RecordScope

	/**
	 * Validator for the complete record structure.
	 *
	 * Should validate the entire record including `id` and `typeName` fields.
	 * Use validators like T.object, T.string, etc.
	 */
	validator: T.Validatable<any>

	/**
	 * Optional migration sequence for handling schema evolution over time.
	 *
	 * Can be a full MigrationSequence or a simplified TLPropsMigrations format.
	 * If not provided, an empty migration sequence will be created automatically.
	 */
	migrations?: MigrationSequence | TLPropsMigrations

	/**
	 * Optional factory function that returns default property values for new records.
	 *
	 * Called when creating new records to provide initial values for any properties
	 * not explicitly provided during creation.
	 */
	// eslint-disable-next-line tldraw/method-signature-style
	createDefaultProperties?: () => Record<string, unknown>
}

units.name: createCustomRecordType
units.source:
* @param typeName - The unique type name for this record type
 * @param config - Configuration for the custom record type
 * @returns A RecordType instance that can be used to create and manage records

detail.name: createCustomRecordType
preconditions: typeName identifies the unique custom record type.
config provides the configuration for the custom record type.
postconditions: Returns a RecordType instance associated with the supplied type name and configuration.
detail.summary: Creates a custom record type from a unique type name and its configuration, returning a RecordType instance for creating and managing records.

units.name: processCustomRecordMigrations

detail.name: processCustomRecordMigrations
detail.signature: export function processCustomRecordMigrations(records: Record<string, CustomRecordInfo>): MigrationSequence[]
preconditions: Each record value conforms to CustomRecordInfo.
When a full MigrationSequence is supplied, its sequenceId must equal `com.tldraw.${typeName}` for the corresponding record type.
postconditions: Returns one MigrationSequence for each entry in records, in Object.entries(records) iteration order.
Each generated sequence has sequenceId `com.tldraw.${typeName}` and retroactive set to true.
A missing migrations configuration produces an empty migration sequence.
A full MigrationSequence configuration is returned unchanged after sequenceId validation.
A sequence-format migration configuration is converted into record-scoped migrations filtered to the corresponding typeName.
invariants: Generated migration sequence IDs are derived from the record type name using the prefix `com.tldraw.`.
Converted migration filters accept only records whose typeName equals the enclosing record type name.
Migration IDs and dependsOn values are preserved when converting sequence-format migrations.
A truthy result from an up or down migration callback is returned; a falsy result is converted to undefined.
edgeCases: An empty records object returns an empty array.
A record with no migrations produces a retroactive sequence with an empty sequence.
A sequence-format migration entry without an `id` is preserved without adding record scope or a typeName filter.
A sequence-format migration with a down value that is not a function produces a converted migration with down set to undefined.
A full MigrationSequence whose sequenceId does not match the derived ID causes an assertion failure instead of being returned.

raises: Assertion error from the sequenceId consistency check
errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Throws when a supplied full MigrationSequence has a sequenceId different from the derived `com.tldraw.${typeName}` value.

detail.summary: Converts custom record migration configurations into migration sequences consumable by the store system. It creates retroactive empty or converted sequences when needed and preserves validated full migration sequences.

specLiterals.role: Defines the sequenceId assigned to each custom record type.

specLiterals.role: Assertion error message for a full migration sequence whose ID does not match the derived custom record sequence ID.
Scope assigned to converted identified migrations.

specTests.then: It returns one retroactive MigrationSequence with sequenceId `com.tldraw.Widget` and an empty migration sequence.

specTests.when: The returned migration's filter is applied to records with typeName `Widget` and to records with another typeName.
specTests.then: The filter accepts the `Widget` record and rejects the record with another typeName; the converted migration has scope `record`.
The call throws an assertion error containing `sequenceId mismatch for Widget custom record migrations`.

detail.name: createCustomRecordMigrationSequence
detail.signature: function createCustomRecordMigrationSequence<T extends UnknownRecord>(config: { sequence: Migration<T>[] }): MigrationSequence<T>
preconditions: The configuration contains a sequence of valid custom-record migrations.
Migration identifiers are valid custom-record migration identifiers.
postconditions: Returns a migration sequence containing the supplied migrations in their original order.
Each migration remains associated with its original identifier and upgrade behavior.
invariants: The sequence represents migrations for the custom-record type described by the supplied migration identifiers.
edgeCases: An empty sequence produces an empty migration sequence.
Multiple migrations are retained in the order supplied.
A migration sequence containing an invalid identifier is not made valid by this function; validation or failure follows the underlying migration-sequence contract.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Invalid migration configuration or identifiers follow the underlying migration-sequence validation behavior.

detail.summary: Creates a migration sequence for custom records from an ordered collection of record migrations. The resulting sequence preserves the supplied migration definitions and their execution order.

units.source:
* @param typeName - The type name of the custom record
 * @param id - Optional custom ID suffix. If not provided, a unique ID will be generated
 * @returns A properly formatted record ID
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts

detail.name: createCustomRecordId
detail.signature: function createCustomRecordId(typeName: string, id?: string): string
preconditions: typeName is a string identifying the custom record type.
postconditions: The returned value is a record identifier composed of the type name, a colon separator, and either the supplied suffix or a generated unique suffix.
When id is supplied, its value is preserved in the returned identifier.
invariants: The type name and identifier suffix are separated by exactly one colon in the returned format.
A missing id produces a newly generated unique identifier suffix.
edgeCases: When id is provided as an empty string, the empty suffix is used rather than generating a unique suffix.
When id is omitted or undefined, a unique suffix is generated.
The returned identifier retains the supplied typeName as its prefix.
detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns a string in the form `${typeName}:${id}` when id is supplied, or `${typeName}:${generatedUniqueId}` when id is omitted.
detail.summary: Creates a custom record identifier by combining the record type name with an optional custom suffix. When no suffix is supplied, it generates a unique suffix.

specLiterals.role: Separates the custom record type name from its identifier suffix.

specTests.then: The result begins with "shape:" and contains a generated unique suffix.

units.name: isCustomRecordId
units.source:
* Type guard to check if a string is a valid ID for a specific custom record type.
 *
 * @param typeName - The type name to check against
 * @param id - The string to check

detail.name: isCustomRecordId
detail.signature: isCustomRecordId<T extends UnknownRecord>(typeName: T['typeName'], id: string): id is RecordId<T>
preconditions: typeName is a custom record type name.
postconditions: Returns true only when id has the specified type name followed by the custom record ID delimiter.
When true, id is type-narrowed to RecordId<T>.
invariants: The type-name prefix is compared at the beginning of id.
The input strings are not mutated.
edgeCases: An id beginning with the specified type name and delimiter is accepted.
An id with a different type-name prefix is rejected.
An id that does not contain the required delimiter immediately after the type name is rejected.

errorPolicy.returnsOnError: Returns false for an ID that does not match the specified custom record type.

detail.summary: Determines whether a string is a valid custom record ID for the specified record type and narrows matching IDs to RecordId<T>.

specLiterals.role: Defines the required custom record ID prefix format.

specTests.then: The function returns true and the ID is recognized as a RecordId for that custom type.

units.name: isCustomRecord

detail.name: isCustomRecord
detail.signature: function isCustomRecord(record: TLRecord): record is TLCustomRecord
preconditions: The argument is a record value compatible with TLRecord.
postconditions: Returns a boolean indicating whether the record is a custom record.
When the result is true, the record is narrowed to TLCustomRecord for TypeScript callers.
invariants: The function does not mutate the supplied record.
edgeCases: A record that does not satisfy the custom-record shape returns false.
A valid custom record returns true.
detail.summary: Acts as a type guard that identifies whether a record is a custom record.
